react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological system: androgen and estrogen metabolism is the dominant affected pathway across every analytical lens applied. In the KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR), pathway hsa00140 ('Steroid hormone biosynthesis') ranks first with p = 5.77 × 10⁻⁷, driven by six steroid metabolites — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), androstenedione (C00280), estrone (C00468), estradiol (C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — hitting a 87-compound KEGG roster. The multi-database ORA (RaMP) reports the equivalent KEGG map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at rank 2 (FDR = 5.81 × 10⁻¹⁸) with identical six-compound overlap; SMPDB pathway SMP00068 ('Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism') and SMP00356 ('17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency') tie at ranks 0–1 with fold enrichment of 1501× and the same six metabolites. Reactome R-HSA-196071 ('Metabolism of steroid hormones') follows at rank 4 (FDR = 5.12 × 10⁻¹⁷). The m/z-direct mummichog network also returns 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' as its top hit (p = 2.52 × 10⁻⁴), with perfect 14-of-14 input overlap against that network module, confirming these six steroids as pathway drivers. A secondary cluster of disaccharide/sugar pathways (sucrose, starch-and-sucrose metabolism, galactose) appears at p ≈ 0.05 in mummichog and is likely a secondary perturbation. Caffeine maps to the caffeine metabolism pathway (hsa00232, p = 0.049) as a single-hit outlier. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: the treatment group perturbs central steroid hormone biosynthesis, with six C19/C18 steroids collectively producing one of the most statistically significant pathway signals in metabolomics enrichment.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Over-representation analysis across three paradigms converges on steroid metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP multi-database ORA identified Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, FDR=5.81e-18) as the top hit, with six steroids deviating in parallel: dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, 17β-estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone. Reactome enrichment independently recovered Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=5.12e-17) as the sixth-ranked pathway, providing cross-paradigm validation. WikiPathways Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496, FDR=1.60e-16) captures five of these steroids and is ranked seventh by RaMP. The six steroids co-occur in Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism and in Metabolism of steroid hormones, indicating coordinated disruption of the androgen-to-estrogen conversion axis. Estrone and 17β-estradiol represent opposing ends of the aromatase reaction, while androstenedione and dihydrotestosterone bracket the 5α-reductase step. Three non-steroid metabolites (caffeine, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, sucrose) were detected but did not enrich any pathway, suggesting they are noise or treatment-specific but mechanistically peripheral. The four confirmed driver steroids are dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, and 17β-estradiol, all resolved by RaMP into the androgen-estrogen metabolic hub.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Over-representation analysis across three paradigms converges on steroid metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP multi-database ORA identified Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, FDR=5.81e-18) as the top hit, with six steroids deviating in parallel: dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, 17β-estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone. Reactome enrichment independently recovered Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=5.12e-17) as the sixth-ranked pathway, providing cross-paradigm validation. WikiPathways Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496, FDR=1.60e-16) captures five of these steroids and is ranked seventh by RaMP. The six steroids co-occur in Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism and in Metabolism of steroid hormones, indicating coordinated disruption of the androgen-to-estrogen conversion axis. Estrone and 17β-estradiol represent opposing ends of the aromatase reaction, while androstenedione and dihydrotestosterone bracket the 5α-reductase step. Three non-steroid metabolites (caffeine, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, sucrose) were detected but did not enrich any pathway, suggesting they are noise or treatment-specific but mechanistically peripheral. The four confirmed driver steroids are dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, and 17β-estradiol, all resolved by RaMP into the androgen-estrogen metabolic hub.
